solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nomadic lot dwell in vessel

indicators.note: the word for dwelling is placed within the boat word

parts.note: a tug is a small towing vessel
to dwell is to exist or be, giving the verb form are

explanation.surface: A band of wanderers living aboard a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuareg are a Berber people of the Sahara, traditionally nomadic herders, so they are a wandering group.

clue.text: Retired medic, a writer, wearing jacket in January in danger

indicators.note: the outer letters wear the reversed group like clothing, wrapped round it
the jacket of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
retired means drawn back, so the group of medic, a and writer runs backwards

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: A retired doctor and an author, in a coat in midwinter, are at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reverses the whole group of medic, a and writer, not just the medic; 'jacket in January' means the month's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy is a synonym for peril or risk of harm.

clue.text: Perhaps, darken London suburb that's not half joyous

parts.note: read whimsically, de-light means take the light away, and 'Perhaps' flags the playful reading

indicators.note: only half of the district name is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: Fulham is a district of south-west London

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to dim a joyless part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' warns that DE-LIGHT is a punning way to say darken. FULHAM is a district of west London; 'not half' keeps FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Delightful and joyous are near-synonyms, both meaning giving great pleasure.

clue.text: Aim of undergraduate's journey in part?

definitions.meaning: a student's studies head towards a university qualification, the destination of the journey

explanation.surface: Asking what a student's travels through university are partly for.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to some extent, and literally names a student heading for a qualification.

clue.text: Boss in reading area overlooking yard

indicators.note: to overlook is to leave out, so the yard letter is ignored

parts.note: a study is a room for reading and work

explanation.surface: A manager working in a library that has a view of a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is the decorative knob sense, not a manager; 'overlooking' means ignoring, not looking down on.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a raised knob on a surface, and a boss is the same kind of ornamental projection.

clue.text: Pair of goods accepted in sound bargain

indicators.note: the two letters are taken into the word for healthy

parts.note: sound in the sense of healthy, as in hale and hearty
g is the abbreviation for good, so two of them

explanation.surface: Two items taken as part of a solid deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noise or a good deal; it is healthy, HALE. 'bargain' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to negotiate over price, which is what haggling means.

clue.text: Businessman with cunning and energy repeatedly showing skill in exchange

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
art in the sense of craft or guile

indicators.note: the energy letter is given more than once, here twice

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A salesman whose craft and drive keep showing in negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty reply, a talent shown in conversation's back-and-forth.

clue.text: Unproductive former tennis star entering America

indicators.note: the player's name goes into the country letters

parts.note: US is the United States
Monica Seles, a former world number one

explanation.surface: A retired tennis player arriving in the States achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Useless and unproductive both describe something that yields no result.

clue.text: Confirm meal for a shark?

definitions.meaning: to ratify, as by stamping a document
a marine mammal that great whites prey on

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is food for a predatory fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To seal a deal is to confirm it, and the sea mammal is a shark's prey.

clue.text: Old area getting income to cover cold snack?

indicators.note: the earnings word covers the cold letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the take is money taken in
c is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An old district earning money to pay for a chilled bite.
explanation.definitionFit: An oatcake is a flat oat biscuit often eaten as a light bite, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Regarding and following formal lecture

indicators.note: the conjunction comes after the stiff word

parts.note: re means concerning
prim means stiffly proper

explanation.surface: A query about a formal lecture and what comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand is to rebuke formally, much as one lectures someone for misbehaving.

clue.text: Follow scholar in set of beliefs

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: Adopting an academic's ideology.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a body of doctrine held as authoritative, a creed.

clue.text: It's right to alter measure of thickness

indicators.note: the letters of right are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A claim that it is proper to change a thickness reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the measurement round the middle of something, its circumference.

clue.text: In which there's talk about broadly fully everything principally with time

definitions.text: In which there's talk about broadly fully everything principally with time

indicators.note: the chatter word goes round the initials

parts.note: gas means idle chatter

indicators.note: the first letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: Something where people speak broadly and fully about everything at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is a containment, wrapping the chatter word round the initials; read whole, the clue also describes a long chat session.
explanation.definitionFit: A gabfest is an informal gathering for lengthy chatter on any subject, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Consider marine that's deployed in difficult situation

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for a fix

parts.note: a bind is an awkward predicament

indicators.note: deployed means spread about, so the letters of marine are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thinking about a soldier sent into a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's deployed' rearranges MARINE to EARINM, which goes into B...IND.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in mind is to take it into account, to consider it.

clue.text: A notch is carved out by new bar

indicators.note: carving reshapes, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: A groove is cut into a fresh rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved out' rearranges the letters of A NOTCH IS into STANCHIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright post or bar used as a support.

clue.text: See red arch on holiday, then head out to take in lake

parts.note: arch means knowing or crafty, as is fly in British slang
off work, away

indicators.note: the mixed letters take in the lake letter, enclosing it
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of then and head are mixed

explanation.surface: A sly person on vacation who later loses their head over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges THEN + HEAD; 'to take in' puts L among them, making THEHANDLE. FLY, British slang for sharp or knowing, means the same as arch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for suddenly losing one's temper.

clue.text: Papers held up in matter that's undisputed in cosmetic operation

indicators.note: the turned documents go inside the word for a certainty

parts.note: a fact is something beyond dispute

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: a file is a set of documents

explanation.surface: Documents delayed in a clear-cut case of plastic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'held up' means read upwards, so the papers word is reversed before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is plastic surgery to tighten the skin of the face.

clue.text: Omit excitement in play from back?

parts.note: to drop is to leave out
a kick is a thrill

explanation.surface: Leaving out the thrill when acting out a scene from the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a drop kick, where the ball is kicked as it bounces, is often taken by backs such as fly-halves.

clue.text: Star in silent place found in set of links

indicators.note: the place abbreviation is found within the word for a series of links

parts.note: a chain is a series of connected links

explanation.surface: A celebrity hidden quietly somewhere within a network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silent' is a noun here: a silent film.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was the great comic actor of silent films.

clue.text: Creative when Queen's on board vessel

indicators.note: the royal letters are aboard the artistic word, inside it

parts.note: arty means artistic
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; the apostrophe s stands for is

explanation.surface: An artistic flair shown when the monarch boards a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' is a blood vessel, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An artery is a blood vessel carrying blood from the heart.

clue.text: Merchant's partner in white

definitions.meaning: James ..., film director who partnered producer Ismail Merchant in Merchant ... Productions

explanation.surface: A trader's business associate dressed in white.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour is named after elephant tusk material, and the film director shared a famous partnership with Merchant.

clue.text: Unknown employee heading off for a delivery

parts.note: y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: the first letter of the employee word is removed

parts.note: a worker is an employee

explanation.surface: An anonymous staff member leaving to make a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; a yorker is a ball aimed to land at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A yorker is a type of ball bowled in cricket, and each ball bowled is a delivery.

clue.text: Prayer leader making introduction for Welsh politician

parts.note: I'm is how one introduces oneself, as in I'm Bob
AM, Assembly Member of the Welsh Assembly

explanation.surface: A cleric introducing a member of the Welsh Assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque.

clue.text: Service finished providing respite

parts.note: a let is a tennis serve that clips the net and is replayed
up as in time's up, over

explanation.surface: The end of a serving session brings relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing, a break from pressure.

clue.text: Top dog reportedly

indicators.note: the dog's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a peke is a Pekingese dog

explanation.surface: Word is that this is the best hound.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is a summit or highest point.

clue.text: One with domestic charge could be former PM's successful aide?

parts.note: Sir Alec Douglas-Home, British Prime Minister 1963-64
a maker is one who makes someone, as a kingmaker does

explanation.surface: Asking whether a household manager might be an old premier's effective assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas-Home is pronounced 'Hume', so the name hides its spelling. A maker of someone is what makes them successful.
explanation.definitionFit: A homemaker runs a household, so housework is that person's responsibility.

clue.text: Artist featured in US film in a mess

indicators.note: the artist appears inside the film title

parts.note: Fargo, the 1996 Coen brothers film
RA, Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter appearing in an American movie that turns out chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble, a hotchpotch.

clue.text: Male and female singer (loveless male one) offering means for observation

parts.note: Yoko Ono

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, which is dropped

parts.note: a male singer, Nat King Cole

explanation.surface: A man and a woman vocalist plus a solitary unloved man, offering a way of watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to singer, so 'male one' is a male singer, COLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single eyeglass, a device for seeing.
